primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Chronic exposure to inhaled toxins causes airway inflammation and/or emphysematous destruction, producing persistent expiratory airflow limitation that is not fully reversible.
vignette: A 67-year-old man with a 50-pack-year smoking history has chronic cough, progressive dyspnea, and post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC of 0.58.
distractor_notes: Asthma usually shows variable and substantially reversible airflow obstruction.
Pulmonary fibrosis causes restrictive physiology with preserved or increased FEV1/FVC.
Pulmonary embolism causes acute perfusion defects, not chronic obstructive spirometry.
Cystic-fibrosis bronchiectasis usually presents much earlier and has a different disease context.
key_expl: Persistent post-bronchodilator airflow obstruction in a heavy smoker is classic COPD.
objective: Recognize COPD from exposure history and fixed obstructive spirometry.

sources.title: COPD
sources.support: NHLBI describes COPD as persistent airflow limitation commonly related to smoking.

sources.title: COPD
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes chronic bronchitis and emphysema as causes of persistent airflow obstruction.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Progressive interstitial fibrosis stiffens the lungs, reducing compliance and diffusion capacity and producing a restrictive ventilatory defect.
vignette: A 72-year-old man has progressive exertional dyspnea, dry cough, bibasilar fine inspiratory crackles, and clubbing. High-resolution CT shows peripheral basilar reticulation and honeycombing.
distractor_notes: COPD causes obstructive physiology and often hyperinflation rather than basilar honeycombing.
Asthma is episodic and reversible, without fibrotic honeycombing.
Pulmonary embolism is acute and vascular.
Pneumonia usually causes fever and focal or multifocal infiltrates, not chronic peripheral fibrosis.
key_expl: Progressive dyspnea, bibasilar crackles, clubbing, and basilar subpleural honeycombing indicate idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
objective: Recognize idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis from chronic restrictive symptoms and characteristic CT findings.

sources.title: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
sources.support: NHLBI describes IPF as progressive lung scarring with dyspnea, dry cough, and characteristic imaging.

sources.title: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes progressive fibrotic lung disease with breathing difficulty.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Destruction of alveolar septa reduces alveolar-capillary surface area, lowering diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide.
vignette: A patient with emphysema has reduced DLCO.
lead: Which structural change most directly causes this reduction?
distractors: Increased alveolar wall thickness from fibrosis only
distractor_notes: Fibrosis can also reduce diffusion but is not the defining structural change in emphysema.
Higher hemoglobin tends to increase measured DLCO.
Bronchoconstriction affects airflow more than gas-transfer surface area.
Greater capillary blood volume tends to increase gas uptake rather than reduce DLCO.
key_expl: Emphysematous destruction reduces the area available for gas diffusion, lowering DLCO.
objective: Connect alveolar septal destruction in emphysema with reduced DLCO.

sources.title: Emphysema
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes destruction of alveolar walls in emphysema.

sources.title: COPD
sources.support: NHLBI describes damage to alveoli in emphysema and impaired gas exchange.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Acute hypoventilation raises arterial carbon dioxide, shifting the bicarbonate buffer equilibrium toward carbonic acid and lowering pH.
vignette: After opioid overdose, a patient has pH 7.24 and PaCO2 68 mm Hg with only a small rise in bicarbonate.
lead: Which primary acid-base disorder is present?
distractor_notes: Chronic respiratory acidosis shows greater renal bicarbonate retention.
Metabolic acidosis has low bicarbonate as the primary disturbance.
Respiratory alkalosis has low PaCO2.
Metabolic alkalosis has elevated bicarbonate as the primary disturbance.
key_expl: Acute hypoventilation causes primary CO2 retention and respiratory acidosis before full renal compensation develops.
objective: Identify acute respiratory acidosis from blood gas data.

sources.title: Respiratory acidosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes hypoventilation and carbon dioxide retention as causes of respiratory acidosis.

sources.title: Blood Gases
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes arterial blood gases as measuring pH, carbon dioxide, and oxygen.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Immune complexes formed after nephritogenic streptococcal infection deposit in glomeruli, activate complement, and cause acute nephritic syndrome.
vignette: An 8-year-old boy develops cola-colored urine, periorbital edema, and hypertension 2 weeks after impetigo. Urinalysis shows red-cell casts and serum C3 is low.
distractor_notes: IgA nephropathy typically causes hematuria during or immediately after mucosal infection rather than after a latent period.
Minimal change disease causes nephrotic proteinuria without red-cell casts.
Cystitis causes dysuria and nonglomerular hematuria.
Alport syndrome is inherited and associated with hearing loss.
key_expl: Acute nephritic syndrome after a 1–3 week latent period following streptococcal infection with low complement is classic PSGN.
objective: Differentiate PSGN from IgA nephropathy using timing and complement levels.

sources.title: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes PSGN as glomerular inflammation after streptococcal infection.

sources.title: About Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis
sources.support: CDC describes PSGN as a delayed immune complication of group A streptococcal infection.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autoantibodies against alpha-3 chains of type IV collagen in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes cause rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis and pulmonary hemorrhage.
vignette: A 25-year-old man has hemoptysis, rapidly rising creatinine, and red-cell casts. Kidney biopsy shows linear IgG deposition along the glomerular basement membrane.
lead: Which target antigen is most likely involved?
correct: Type IV collagen in basement membranes
distractor_notes: Anti-dsDNA antibodies are associated with lupus nephritis.
PR3-ANCA is associated with granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
MPO-ANCA is associated with microscopic polyangiitis and related vasculitides.
Desmoglein antibodies cause pemphigus vulgaris.
key_expl: Anti-GBM disease targets type IV collagen in alveolar and glomerular basement membranes.
objective: Identify type IV collagen as the autoantigen in anti-GBM disease.

sources.title: Goodpasture syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes Goodpasture syndrome as antibodies attacking lung and kidney basement membranes.

sources.title: Anti-GBM disease
sources.support: NIDDK describes antibodies to type IV collagen in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Generalized proximal tubular dysfunction causes urinary wasting of bicarbonate, phosphate, glucose, amino acids, and uric acid.
vignette: A child has growth failure, metabolic acidosis, glucosuria despite normal serum glucose, phosphaturia, and generalized aminoaciduria.
lead: Which nephron segment is primarily dysfunctional?
distractor_notes: Thick ascending limb defects cause Bartter physiology.
Distal convoluted tubule defects cause Gitelman syndrome.
Collecting duct defects cause water-balance or potassium disorders.
Podocyte injury causes proteinuria rather than generalized solute wasting.
key_expl: Fanconi syndrome is a generalized proximal tubular reabsorptive defect.
objective: Localize Fanconi syndrome to the proximal tubule.

sources.title: Fanconi syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes Fanconi syndrome as defective proximal tubular reabsorption of multiple substances.

sources.title: Renal Tubular Acidosis
sources.support: NIDDK describes proximal bicarbonate wasting as a cause of renal tubular acidosis.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of the thiazide-sensitive Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule causes salt wasting, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesemia, and hypocalciuria.
vignette: A 19-year-old woman has muscle cramps, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, hypomagnesemia, high renin and aldosterone, and low urinary calcium.
correct: Na-Cl cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule
distractors: Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
distractor_notes: NKCC2 defects cause Bartter syndrome and often hypercalciuria.
ENaC loss causes pseudohypoaldosteronism.
SGLT defects cause renal glucosuria.
Aquaporin-2 defects cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
key_expl: Gitelman syndrome mimics chronic thiazide effect through loss of the distal Na-Cl cotransporter.
objective: Differentiate Gitelman from Bartter syndrome using transporter location and urinary calcium.

sources.title: Gitelman syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes SLC12A3-related loss of the distal Na-Cl cotransporter.

sources.title: SLC12A3 gene
sources.support: SLC12A3 encodes the thiazide-sensitive Na-Cl cotransporter of the distal convoluted tubule.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Elevated extracellular potassium partially depolarizes cardiac myocytes, alters sodium-channel availability, and produces progressive ECG changes including peaked T waves and QRS widening.
vignette: A patient with acute kidney injury has serum potassium of 7.2 mEq/L and tall peaked T waves.
lead: Which electrolyte disturbance best explains the ECG finding?
distractor_notes: Hypokalemia classically causes flattened T waves and U waves.
Hypercalcemia shortens the QT interval.
Hypocalcemia prolongs the QT interval.
Hypernatremia does not characteristically cause peaked T waves.
key_expl: Peaked T waves in renal failure strongly indicate hyperkalemia.
objective: Recognize hyperkalemia from classic ECG changes.

sources.title: High potassium level
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes hyperkalemia as causing potentially dangerous cardiac electrical abnormalities.

sources.title: Potassium Blood Test
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes kidney disease as a cause of elevated potassium.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Reduced perfusion pressure in a stenotic renal artery stimulates renin release, increasing angiotensin II and aldosterone and causing secondary hypertension.
vignette: A 68-year-old man has refractory hypertension and an abdominal bruit. Imaging shows severe unilateral renal artery stenosis.
lead: Which hormone is most directly increased by the affected kidney?
distractor_notes: ANP is secreted by atria in response to stretch and opposes RAAS.
Calcitonin regulates calcium metabolism.
Insulin is pancreatic.
TSH is pituitary and unrelated to renal perfusion.
key_expl: Renal hypoperfusion stimulates juxtaglomerular renin secretion and activates RAAS.
objective: Explain renovascular hypertension through renal hypoperfusion and renin release.

sources.title: Renal artery stenosis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes renal artery narrowing as a cause of renovascular hypertension.

sources.title: Renovascular Hypertension
sources.support: NIDDK describes reduced renal blood flow leading to hormonal activation and hypertension.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Malignant renal tubular epithelial cells can produce hematuria, flank mass or pain, and paraneoplastic hormones such as erythropoietin.
vignette: A 62-year-old man has painless hematuria, weight loss, and a left renal mass. Hematocrit is unexpectedly elevated.
distractor_notes: Bladder cancer can cause hematuria but does not explain a renal mass with erythrocytosis.
Wilms tumor occurs mainly in young children.
Pyelonephritis causes fever and flank pain with infection findings.
PKD causes bilateral cystic enlargement rather than a solid unilateral malignant mass.
key_expl: A renal mass with hematuria and paraneoplastic erythrocytosis is classic RCC.
objective: Recognize RCC and its erythropoietin-associated paraneoplastic effect.

sources.title: Kidney Cancer
sources.support: NCI describes hematuria, flank symptoms, and renal tumors.

sources.title: Kidney cancer
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes renal cell carcinoma as the common adult kidney cancer.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Ascending bacterial infection of the renal pelvis and parenchyma produces fever, flank pain, pyuria, and often white-cell casts.
vignette: A 27-year-old woman has fever, nausea, dysuria, and right costovertebral angle tenderness. Urinalysis shows pyuria and white-cell casts.
distractor_notes: Cystitis causes lower urinary symptoms without fever, flank pain, or white-cell casts.
A stone may cause colicky flank pain and hematuria but not pyuria with WBC casts unless infected.
Glomerulonephritis causes red-cell casts and proteinuria.
Interstitial cystitis is chronic and noninfectious.
key_expl: Fever, CVA tenderness, pyuria, and WBC casts indicate renal parenchymal infection.
objective: Differentiate pyelonephritis from lower urinary infection.

sources.title: Kidney infection
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes kidney infection with fever, flank pain, and urinary symptoms.

sources.title: Bladder Infection vs Kidney Infection
sources.support: NIDDK describes pyelonephritis as infection of the kidney with systemic symptoms.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Dihydrotestosterone-driven stromal and glandular hyperplasia in the periurethral transition zone narrows the prostatic urethra and causes bladder outlet obstruction.
vignette: A 68-year-old man has urinary hesitancy, weak stream, and nocturia. Prostate is symmetrically enlarged and smooth.
lead: Which androgen most directly promotes prostatic growth in this condition?
distractor_notes: Estrogen may influence prostate biology but DHT is the key potent androgen driving prostatic growth.
Cortisol does not mediate BPH growth.
Aldosterone regulates sodium balance.
DHEAS is an adrenal androgen precursor and is not the principal intraprostatic growth signal.
key_expl: 5-alpha-reductase converts testosterone to DHT, which strongly stimulates prostatic tissue growth.
objective: Connect BPH pathophysiology with DHT signaling.

sources.title: Enlarged Prostate (BPH)
sources.support: NIDDK describes BPH as noncancerous prostate enlargement causing urinary obstruction.

sources.title: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes hormonal influence and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor treatment in BPH.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: H pylori colonizes gastric mucus using urease, alters mucosal defense and gastrin signaling, and promotes chronic inflammation leading to peptic ulcer disease.
vignette: A 43-year-old man has recurrent epigastric pain. Gastric biopsy shows curved gram-negative organisms and a strongly positive urease test.
lead: Which microbial enzyme helps the organism survive gastric acidity?
distractors: Catalase only as the defining gastric survival mechanism
distractor_notes: Coagulase is characteristic of S aureus and is unrelated to gastric colonization.
H pylori may have catalase, but urease-generated ammonia is the classic mechanism aiding survival in acidic gastric mucus.
Beta-lactamase is an antibiotic-resistance enzyme, not the defining acid-buffering mechanism.
Hyaluronidase promotes tissue spread in some bacteria but does not explain H pylori gastric survival.
key_expl: H pylori urease generates ammonia from urea, locally buffering gastric acid.
objective: Identify urease as a key H pylori virulence factor.

sources.title: Helicobacter pylori infections
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes H pylori as a cause of peptic ulcers and urease-based testing.

sources.title: H. pylori and Peptic Ulcers
sources.support: NIDDK describes H pylori infection as a major cause of peptic ulcer disease.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Premature intrapancreatic activation of digestive enzymes causes pancreatic autodigestion, inflammation, and elevated serum lipase.
vignette: A 41-year-old woman has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and serum lipase three times the upper limit of normal after a fatty meal. Ultrasound shows gallstones.
distractor_notes: Cholecystitis causes right upper quadrant pain and gallbladder inflammation but does not typically cause marked lipase elevation with back-radiating epigastric pain.
Perforated ulcer causes sudden peritoneal signs and free air.
Mesenteric ischemia causes severe pain often out of proportion to examination findings.
Acute hepatitis causes transaminase elevation and systemic symptoms rather than classic pancreatitis pain and lipase.
key_expl: Severe back-radiating epigastric pain plus marked lipase elevation indicates acute pancreatitis.
objective: Recognize gallstone-associated acute pancreatitis.

sources.title: Pancreatitis
sources.support: NIDDK describes acute pancreatitis with severe upper abdominal pain and gallstones as a common cause.

sources.title: Acute pancreatitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes acute pancreatitis and elevated pancreatic enzymes.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Persistent cystic duct obstruction by a gallstone causes gallbladder distention and inflammation.
vignette: A 48-year-old woman has fever and persistent right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal. Inspiration during deep palpation of the right upper quadrant abruptly stops because of pain.
distractor_notes: Biliary colic is transient obstruction without sustained inflammatory fever and Murphy sign.
Ascending cholangitis typically includes jaundice and systemic infection from common bile duct obstruction.
Pancreatitis causes epigastric pain radiating to the back and elevated lipase.
Hepatic abscess has a different focal hepatic infectious pattern.
key_expl: Persistent RUQ pain, fever, and positive Murphy sign indicate acute cholecystitis.
objective: Differentiate acute cholecystitis from biliary colic.

sources.title: Acute cholecystitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes cystic duct obstruction causing gallbladder inflammation, RUQ pain, and fever.

sources.title: Gallstones
sources.support: NIDDK describes gallstones as a cause of cholecystitis when they obstruct gallbladder outflow.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons reduces nitric oxide-mediated lower esophageal sphincter relaxation and causes aperistalsis.
vignette: A 36-year-old man has progressive dysphagia to both solids and liquids. Barium study shows a dilated esophagus with distal bird-beak narrowing.
lead: Loss of which neurotransmitter-mediated function most directly causes the disorder?
correct: Nitric oxide-mediated relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter
distractor_notes: Achalasia is due to loss of inhibitory myenteric signaling, not failure of skeletal muscle cholinergic transmission.
Dopamine is not the principal LES inhibitory transmitter.
Histamine regulates gastric acid secretion.
Secretin regulates pancreatic bicarbonate.
key_expl: Achalasia results from loss of inhibitory myenteric neurons, especially nitric oxide signaling, preventing LES relaxation.
objective: Explain achalasia through loss of inhibitory myenteric neurotransmission.

sources.title: Achalasia
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes achalasia as impaired relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter with absent normal peristalsis.

sources.title: Achalasia
sources.support: NIDDK describes nerve dysfunction in the esophagus leading to impaired LES relaxation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Germline APC loss impairs beta-catenin degradation, activating Wnt signaling and producing hundreds to thousands of colorectal adenomas with near-certain cancer risk without intervention.
vignette: A 19-year-old man has hundreds of adenomatous polyps throughout the colon. His father had colon cancer at age 32.
lead: Which signaling abnormality most directly results from the underlying mutation?
distractor_notes: RET activation, not inhibition, causes MEN2.
Mismatch repair defects cause Lynch syndrome, which generally does not produce hundreds of polyps.
APC loss increases growth signaling rather than reducing RAS.
p53 activation suppresses tumors rather than driving FAP.
key_expl: APC normally promotes beta-catenin degradation; APC loss increases Wnt/beta-catenin transcriptional signaling.
objective: Connect FAP with APC loss and increased beta-catenin signaling.
clues: very early family history of colon cancer

sources.title: Familial adenomatous polyposis
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes APC mutations as causing FAP and extensive colorectal adenomas.

sources.title: APC gene
sources.support: APC helps regulate beta-catenin and cell growth.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Inherited mismatch-repair gene defects cause microsatellite instability and rapid accumulation of replication errors, predisposing to colorectal and endometrial cancers.
vignette: A 39-year-old woman has endometrial cancer and a strong family history of early colorectal cancer. Tumor testing shows microsatellite instability.
distractors: Base excision repair of uracil only
distractor_notes: Nucleotide excision repair defects cause xeroderma pigmentosum.
Homologous recombination defects are associated with BRCA-related cancer susceptibility.
Base excision repair handles small base lesions and is not the classic Lynch pathway.
Telomere maintenance is not the defining defect in Lynch syndrome.
key_expl: Lynch syndrome is caused by germline defects in DNA mismatch-repair genes such as MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2.
objective: Associate microsatellite instability with mismatch-repair deficiency in Lynch syndrome.

sources.title: Lynch syndrome
sources.support: MedlinePlus Genetics describes Lynch syndrome as caused by mismatch-repair gene defects.

sources.title: MLH1 gene
sources.support: MLH1 participates in DNA mismatch repair.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: Continuous mucosal inflammation begins in the rectum and extends proximally through the colon, causing bloody diarrhea and increased colorectal cancer risk.
vignette: A 26-year-old woman has months of bloody diarrhea and urgency. Colonoscopy shows continuous friable inflammation beginning at the rectum and extending through the sigmoid colon.
distractor_notes: Crohn disease usually has skip lesions and can involve the entire GI tract with transmural disease.
Celiac disease causes malabsorption in the small intestine.
IBS does not cause visible mucosal inflammation or bleeding.
Diverticulitis causes focal abdominal pain and inflammation rather than chronic continuous proctocolitis.
key_expl: Continuous rectum-based inflammatory colitis with bloody diarrhea is classic ulcerative colitis.
objective: Differentiate ulcerative colitis from Crohn disease by distribution and depth.

sources.title: Ulcerative Colitis
sources.support: NIDDK describes ulcerative colitis as continuous inflammatory disease of the colon beginning in the rectum.

sources.title: Ulcerative colitis
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes bloody diarrhea and colonic inflammation.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: After recovery from natural HBV infection, HBsAg disappears while anti-HBs and anti-HBc IgG remain detectable.
vignette: A patient has negative HBsAg, positive anti-HBs, and positive total anti-HBc.
correct: Past natural infection with recovery and immunity
distractor_notes: A susceptible person lacks both surface antigen and antibodies.
Vaccination produces anti-HBs without anti-HBc because vaccine contains surface antigen only.
Acute infection has HBsAg and often anti-HBc IgM.
Chronic infection has persistent HBsAg.
key_expl: Anti-HBs plus anti-HBc with absent HBsAg indicates resolved natural HBV infection.
objective: Interpret hepatitis B serology patterns.

sources.title: Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Hepatitis B
sources.support: CDC describes HBV serologic patterns including resolved infection and vaccine immunity.

sources.title: Hepatitis B
sources.support: MedlinePlus describes blood testing for hepatitis B infection and immunity.
